request.instructions: You are an orchestrator agent that may delegate to child agents. Use graph__propose_spawn to propose a child when decomposition genuinely reduces risk or effort. Set each child's priority and budget_share to reflect how much that subtask matters. Use graph__request_skip_context to let a child see an ancestor's findings directly. After delegating, synthesize the children's findings into one final answer. State your final answer explicitly on the last line, prefixed with 'Answer:'.

messages.content: Produce a rigorous technical brief on database storage and transaction internals. For EACH of the following areas you must discuss at least three specific named mechanisms in real depth: (1) write-ahead logging, (2) MVCC, (3) LSM trees, (4) B+tree maintenance, (5) two-phase commit, (6) logical clocks, (7) quorum systems, (8) crash recovery . Use precise standard terminology for every mechanism you name. Be exhaustive: a shallow mention of an area does not count as covering it.

response.content: I'll decompose this into two balanced subtasks (areas 1–4: single-node storage/logging internals; areas 5–8: distributed coordination and recovery) and propose child agents for each, then synthesize.

arguments.objective: Write a rigorous technical brief section covering (1) write-ahead logging, (2) MVCC, (3) LSM trees, (4) B+tree maintenance, with at least three precisely named mechanisms per area discussed in depth.
arguments.instructions: For WAL: cover ARIES (LSNs, pageLSN, Dirty Page Table, Transaction Table, CLRs, force/no-force, steal/no-steal), physiological logging, group commit, and log shipping/checkpointing variants. For MVCC: cover PostgreSQL xmin/xmax tuple versioning with vacuum, InnoDB undo-log rollback segments with read views, and Snapshot Isolation vs Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI, Cahill et al., rw-antidependency dangerous structures). For LSM trees: cover memtables/SSTables, leveled vs size-tiered compaction (RocksDB vs Cassandra STCS), bloom filters, fractional cascading / fence pointers, write amplification analysis. For B+trees: cover node splits/merges and rebalancing, Blink-trees (Lehman-Yao right-sibling pointers), latch coupling / lock crabbing, sibling redistribution, and fill factor. Use precise standard terminology throughout.

arguments.objective: Write a rigorous technical brief section covering (5) two-phase commit, (6) logical clocks, (7) quorum systems, (8) crash recovery, with at least three precisely named mechanisms per area discussed in depth.
arguments.instructions: For 2PC: cover prepare/commit phases with presumed-abort and presumed-commit optimizations, blocking on coordinator failure, three-phase commit, and Paxos Commit / consensus-backed coordinators (Spanner's 2PC over Paxos). For logical clocks: cover Lamport scalar clocks, vector clocks (with version vectors for replica divergence), and Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC, CockroachDB) plus TrueTime as contrast. For quorums: cover majority read/write quorums (R+W>N, Dynamo-style sloppy quorums with hinted handoff), Paxos/Raft quorum intersection, flexible quorums (Flexible Paxos), and witness replicas. For crash recovery: cover ARIES three-phase recovery (analysis, redo via repeating history, undo with CLRs), fuzzy checkpointing, shadow paging (System R), and torn-page protection (full_page_writes, InnoDB doublewrite buffer). Use precise standard terminology throughout.
